attempted_claim: For the radial focusing cubic energy-critical NLS i∂_t u + Δu + |u|^2u = 0 on R_t × R^4, does there exist, for every α_0 ∈ R and every ν > 1, a finite-time radial type-II solution with some T < ∞ of the form u(t,x) = e^{i α_0 log(T−t)} λ(t) W(λ(t)x) + η(t,x), λ(t) = (T−t)^(−1/2−ν), where W(x) = (1+|x|^2/8)^(−1), sup_{t<T} ||η(t)||_{Ḣ^1 ∩ Ḣ^2} can be made arbitrarily small, and η(t) converges in Ḣ^1 ∩ Ḣ^2 as t ↑ T?
decisive_failure: No existence or nonexistence proof was obtained: the analysis closed neither a construction nor a rigorous disproof, and the supporting numerics only quantify the formal obstruction scale rather than substituting for threshold-resonant spectral estimates. The negative finding is a bounded-time blockage verdict, not a theorem that the target claim is false.
